findings.detail: The problem repeats earlier questions on the same idea. M2-S07-T1 already tests a subagent that sends every timeout to the coordinator, with the fix of local retry plus propagating only unresolved failures with partial results and attempts. M3-S24-T1 already tests the same reasoning in the support setting with lookup_order timeouts, returning the retrieved orders with the failed calls and the retry attempts. Here the same reasoning leads to correct options C and E: recover transient timeouts locally, and propagate only the unresolved failure with partial results and the attempts made. Wrong option D (leaving out the retrieved data) also repeats M2-S07-T1's wrong option about a status sent without the collected results.

blind_answer.reason: The subagent should keep transient failures it recovered from locally and pass up only the error it could not resolve. That report should include the partial results (the order and customer data it retrieved) and what it already tried (three refund attempts), so the coordinator can decide the next step. A is wrong because these timeouts are transient, not permission errors. B is wrong because raw payloads for all six timeouts repeat the original problem. D is wrong because it drops the partial results the coordinator needs.
